chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdul Aziz ibn al-Muhtadi, who said:

I asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him), saying, 'May I be sacrificed for you! My brother died and I married his wife. So my uncle came and claimed that he had married her secretly. So I asked her about that, and she denied with the utmost denial, saying, 'There was never anything between me and him at all.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Her affirmation is binding upon you, and her denial is binding upon him.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (the contented one), a title for Imam Ali al-Rida (AS)
key_terms.الْمُهْتَدِي: Al-Muhtadi (the guided one), a narrator's name
key_terms.جُعِلْتُ فِدَاكَ: May I be sacrificed for you, a common honorific address to the Imam

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling when a husband and his uncle both claim to have married the same woman, one publicly and one secretly?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia legal principle of 'istishab' (presumption of continuity) applied to marital status, where the wife's denial of a secret marriage is accepted unless the claimant provides proof. Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the burden of proof lies with the uncle to establish the prior secret union, while the husband must accept his wife's testimony regarding her own status, highlighting the evidentiary weight given to the spouse's declaration in contested cases.
